draft_role: Root reviewed actual source/code hashes, selected checkpoint/private HF coverage, full and capped episode denominators and raw generation diagnostics, strict parser/allowlist scope, operational CPU controller command, failure preservation, and MIT licensing. Actual public export and CPU episode execution remain release gates.

model_card.scope: Measure generated calculator JSON requests through strict validation, local add/multiply execution, explicit TOOL_RESULT feedback and final completion, compared against the original finite arithmetic question.
limitations: Arithmetic operand-pair families, including reversed operands and both operations, remain in one split.
done is a protocol signal; correctness is independently compared against the original question.
The finite local allowlist does not establish general agent or arbitrary-code execution ability.
These selected branches initialize fresh models in their actual code; a plan-level sft dependency is not evidence of using SFT or UltraChat weights.

The provided infer.py example generates model text only. Reported completed tool episodes additionally use the experiment's strict JSON parser, finite local add/multiply allowlist, execution and explicit TOOL_RESULT feedback loop; raw checkpoint inference alone does not execute those tools.

The first-action JSON rate counts actions parsed as an object; it does not establish a valid allowlisted call, correct arguments, or a correct completed episode. Fault-injection checks exercise the external parser and finite allowlist, not learned prompt-injection resistance.

Full-protocol completion is 19/20, despite 18/18 executed calls matching the requested parameters. The multiply(9,9) episode receives the correct external result 81 but its generated final JSON contains an extra closing brace and an incorrect value, so the parser rejects it. EOS without illegal control tokens does not establish valid JSON or task correctness.
The one-step cap scores 0/18 arithmetic completions: all 18 calls execute, but the step budget stops before a done reply. This subset excludes the two no-tool COPY questions.

evaluation.task: B: generated JSON calculator requests and completions

protocol.reason: render_chat supports no tool role; the system and training data declare this explicit protocol.

one_step_cap_comparison.method: Original arithmetic test questions only, unchanged model weights, with controller max_steps=1 including a done action.

fault_injection_parser_check.scope: Manually supplied malformed/forbidden JSON inputs test the external parser and allowlist; these are not model generations or a model injection-resistance score.

evaluation.generated_token_count_scope: The original aggregate generated_tokens sums full-protocol and one-step-cap episodes; generation_diagnostics separates them.

training_data.source: Program-generated arithmetic tool JSON/protocol conversations; tool results serialized as user TOOL_RESULT content
training_data.modifications: Program-generated controlled records; family-level split before training.

inference.method: Run the existing CPU experiment controller on one program-generated CALC:add(2,3) record. This retains its actual system/user roles, strict JSON validator, finite local allowlist and TOOL_RESULT feedback. Generation uses eval()+no_grad().
commands: python -c "import json; import torch; from types import SimpleNamespace; from tiny_perceptron.training import load_checkpoint; from scripts.course_experiments.applications import _tool_records, _tool_episode; torch.set_num_threads(2); model,_=load_checkpoint('checkpoints/course/tools/model.pt','cpu'); model.eval(); record=next(r for r in _tool_records() if r['operation']=='add' and r['a']==2 and r['b']==3); print(json.dumps(_tool_episode(model,record,SimpleNamespace(device='cpu')),ensure_ascii=False,indent=2))"
inference.scope: One operational trace, not a held-out quality estimate. The top-level infer.py manifest command is a raw model load/generation check with user-only chat; it omits the controller system message and does not execute tools.
